findings.title: Rejected devices remain cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and leaves it there when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Consequently, the first request from an over-limit device fails, but its next request hits the cache and returns nil, allowing Anonymous.Authenticate to admit it for the remainder of the 29-minute cache lifetime. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot observe an admission before its store operation succeeds. Add a service-level test that retries a rejected device.

findings.title: Omitting the device header bypasses the configured limit
findings.body: Authentication now relies on TagDevice to enforce the limit, but TagDevice immediately returns nil when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. An anonymous client can therefore omit this client-controlled header and continue authenticating and accessing APIs even when the device limit is exhausted, without being counted. Enforcement needs a device-identification/admission path that cannot be skipped simply by dropping the header, while explicitly handling requests such as initial page loads that do not carry it.

findings.title: Make the device-count check and admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices runs in a separate database session from the subsequent insert, with no locking or atomic admission mechanism. When the count is one below the limit, simultaneous requests from distinct devices can both observe available capacity and both insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana replicas, and the excess devices remain admitted because subsequent requests are allowed to update existing devices. Serialize the count-and-admit operation across database clients or use an equivalent atomic quota mechanism, and test concurrent admissions at the boundary.
